title: Sponsorship Pitcher
tagline: Creator monetization content + AI that finds sponsors and writes pitches that convert
problem: Small and mid-size creators know sponsorships pay more than ad revenue but do not know which brands sponsor their niche, what to charge or how to pitch. Cold pitches go unanswered and creators undercharge. Sponsor marketplaces mostly serve larger creators.
solution: Creator-monetization content plus an AI tool that scans which brands sponsor similar channels, newsletters and podcasts, builds a target list with contact paths, drafts personalized pitches with the creator's audience stats and suggests a rate from benchmark data. It tracks follow-ups and logs outcomes, which improves the rate benchmarks for everyone. Creators pay per pitch package or a monthly plan.
target_audience: YouTubers with 5K-200K subscribers; podcasters; newsletter writers seeking sponsors
pricing: Free content / $9.99 per sponsor pitch package / $19/mo unlimited
competitors: Passionfroot; YouTube BrandConnect; beehiiv Ad Network; Hashtag Paid
competitor_gap: Small creators below marketplace thresholds get no inbound deals; outbound sponsor discovery plus rate benchmarks fills that
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): My calligraphy looks shaky and inconsistent and I can't figure out why | I don't know which calligraphy pen or style to start with | Practice sheets online are just alphabets with no explanation of technique
unique_data_capture: Sponsor outreach outcomes (response, deal value, CPM) by niche and audience size, building a rate and fit database
commoditization_risk: Medium: Passionfroot, YouTube BrandConnect and newsletter ad networks connect creators with sponsors; general AI drafts pitches
regulatory_notes: FTC endorsement guides require sponsorship disclosure; CAN-SPAM for outreach emails
founder_feasibility: Yes, solo-buildable as a US web/mobile app; Stripe billing.
mvp_features: Sponsor finder + contact researcher + pitch writer + outreach tracker
review_notes: Crowded by marketplaces; viable only if outcome data on sponsor rates becomes the moat.
score_justification: L4 AI matches sponsors and drafts pitches; E4; A4 creators want sponsors; P3 creator communities; M3 sponsor response and rate data; W3 creators pay when deals land

title: Facebook Live Seller Pro
tagline: FB/IG Live selling content + AI that manages orders from chaotic comment streams
problem: Live sellers on Facebook and Instagram in Thailand and the Philippines get hundreds of order comments per stream (CF codes, sizes, typos) and track them by hand or with screenshots. Missed or duplicated orders cause refunds and angry buyers. Sellers spend hours after each live sending bills and chasing payment.
solution: A live-selling order manager that connects to the seller's Facebook, Instagram and TikTok Live, reads comments in real time, and uses AI to parse messy Thai, Tagalog and English order messages into line items. It reserves stock, sends each buyer a bill with a PromptPay or GCash QR, chases unpaid orders and books courier pickups. A post-stream summary shows sales, conversion and best-selling items.
target_audience: Facebook Live sellers; Instagram sellers; social commerce operators in SEA
pricing: Free trial / ฿399 or ₱399 per month / ฿10 per stream on pay-as-you-go
competitors: Page365; Sellsuki; CommentSold; Zort
competitor_gap: Better parsing of messy comments (typos, Thai/Tagalog slang, multiple items), plus TikTok Live support, where incumbents are weaker
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): Comments flood in too fast during live sessions - I miss orders | Customers use abbreviations and local slang I can't parse quickly | Manual order tracking after streams takes 3-4 hours | I lose sales because invoices go out too late
unique_data_capture: Live-stream comment streams labelled with resulting orders, cancellations and payments, learning local slang and code-word ordering patterns (e.g. CF + item code)
commoditization_risk: Medium: Page365 already auto-opens bills when a product is CF'd in Facebook and Instagram lives; Sellsuki and CommentSold compete
regulatory_notes: Meta Platform Terms and app review for live comment access; Thai PDPA and PH Data Privacy Act for buyer data
founder_feasibility: Yes as an offshore SaaS billed by card/e-wallet; local entity or partner needed for some payment rails and B2B invoicing.
mvp_features: Comment parser + order extractor + invoice generator + fulfillment tracker
review_notes: Real demand but Page365 already does the core in Thailand; must win on parsing accuracy and TikTok Live.
score_justification: L4 AI parses free-text comment orders; E3 Meta API permissions and app review; A4 live selling is huge in Thailand and the Philippines; P4 seller Facebook groups; M3 comment-to-order data; W3 sellers pay per month for Page365-type tools

title: COD Collection Helper
tagline: Cash-on-delivery content + AI that reduces failed deliveries and improves collection rates
target_segment: Social commerce sellers using COD in Thailand, Philippines and Indonesia
problem: Cash on delivery is still common in Southeast Asian social commerce, and failed or refused COD deliveries (est. 10-30% for some sellers) cost sellers shipping both ways, tied-up stock and courier penalties. Sellers selling through Facebook, LINE and TikTok cannot tell a real order from a prank or impulse order. Manual confirmation calls take hours a day.
solution: A COD risk and confirmation service for SEA sellers. Each new order gets a risk score from pooled, hashed delivery outcomes, address quality and order patterns. Low-risk orders ship immediately, and higher-risk ones get an automatic WhatsApp or LINE confirmation flow in the buyer's language, an optional small deposit via PromptPay or GCash, and smart delivery-time selection around payday. Sellers see their return-to-sender rate fall in a dashboard. The pooled outcome data makes the score better than any single seller's history.
target_audience: Social commerce sellers using COD in Thailand, Philippines and Indonesia; D2C brands on Facebook, LINE and TikTok; small courier aggregators
pricing: Free up to 100 orders/month / ฿490 or ₱499 per month / enterprise pricing for logistics companies
competitors: OrderOnline.id; Scalev; Courier tools (Flash Express, J&T); Shopify COD apps
competitor_gap: Incumbents automate follow-ups for one seller; none pool outcome data to score risk before shipping in Thailand and the Philippines
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): 15-30% of my COD orders fail delivery and I lose money on returns | Fake orders waste my inventory and delivery costs | I don't know optimal delivery times for different areas | Customers aren't home and refuse redelivery fees
unique_data_capture: Delivery outcomes (delivered, refused, unreachable) by hashed phone, address area, order time and confirmation response across many sellers, forming a COD risk score no single seller or courier dashboard has
commoditization_risk: Medium: OrderOnline.id offers WhatsApp follow-ups and smart logistics in Indonesia, and couriers add their own tools, but a cross-seller risk score is not commoditized
regulatory_notes: Sharing buyer risk data across sellers needs a lawful basis (Thai PDPA legitimate interest or consent, PH Data Privacy Act); avoid blacklisting without appeal; WhatsApp Business API policy
founder_feasibility: Yes as an offshore SaaS billed by card/e-wallet; local entity or partner needed for some payment rails and B2B invoicing. PDPA-compliant data processing agreement needed.
mvp_features: WhatsApp order verification bot | Smart delivery window suggester | Payday cycle optimizer | High-risk order flagger | Automated reminder system
review_notes: Strongest data moat in this batch; main risk is privacy compliance for pooled buyer risk data.
score_justification: L4 AI scores order risk and runs WhatsApp/LINE confirmation flows; E3 courier and chat integrations in 6-8 weeks; A4 COD is still a large share of SEA social commerce and failed deliveries are a known cost; P3 seller groups and courier partnerships; M5 cross-seller delivery outcome data compounds strongly; W4 sellers pay to cut return-to-sender costs

title: Dropship SEA
tagline: SEA dropshipping content + AI that finds local suppliers to avoid long China shipping times
problem: Dropshippers in Southeast Asia who source from China face 2-4 week shipping that buyers hate, which leads to cancellations and bad reviews. Local manufacturers and wholesalers in Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia could ship in days, but they are hard to find, rarely list online and vary in reliability.
solution: A local-supplier finder for SEA dropshippers. Sellers enter a product or link, and the AI matches it to verified regional suppliers, comparing landed cost and delivery time against China sourcing. Suppliers are scored on stock reliability, shipping speed and defect rates reported by sellers. It integrates order forwarding to supplier stock so sellers can fulfil locally without holding inventory. Pricing is per search or a monthly plan.
target_audience: Dropshippers wanting faster delivery; e-commerce entrepreneurs; online business starters in SEA; sellers tired of customer complaints about shipping
pricing: Free dropshipping guides / $15 per supplier search / $79/month for unlimited supplier access
competitors: CJdropshipping; BigSeller; Local dropship platforms; Shopee local warehouses
competitor_gap: Vetted local manufacturers and wholesalers with reliability scores, rather than China stock in regional warehouses
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): Customers hate 2-4 week shipping from China and I get bad reviews | I don't know which products are made locally in SEA | Local suppliers are hard to find without connections | Cost comparison between China and local is complicated
unique_data_capture: Verified SEA supplier catalog with stock reliability, shipping times and defect rates by supplier and SKU
commoditization_risk: Medium: CJdropshipping and BigSeller-linked suppliers offer regional warehouses; local platforms exist in Indonesia and Thailand
regulatory_notes: Product registration and import rules (Thai FDA, BPOM); consumer protection for delivery claims
founder_feasibility: Yes as an offshore SaaS billed by card/e-wallet; local entity or partner needed for some payment rails and B2B invoicing. Supplier vetting needs on-the-ground partners.
mvp_features: Supplier finder + cost comparator + logistics calculator + quality guide
review_notes: Supplier verification is labor-heavy; dropshipping margins are thin.
score_justification: L4 AI matches products to local suppliers; E3 supplier database building; A3; P3 seller groups; M4 verified local supplier data compounds; W3 dropshippers pay for supplier access

title: OFW Money Manager
tagline: OFW content + AI that helps overseas Filipino workers budget and send money home efficiently
target_segment: OFWs in Middle East, Hong Kong, Singapore, and worldwide
problem: Millions of overseas Filipino workers send money home every month but many return with little savings because of family pressure, high remittance fees and no budget. Money advice in Tagalog suited to their host country is scarce. Financial literacy seminars are one-off and easy to forget.
solution: A Tagalog-first money app for OFWs that splits each paycheck into living costs abroad, remittance, emergency fund and goals, compares remittance options for the corridor in real time, and sends reminders before payday. Families back home can see agreed amounts to reduce repeated requests. It offers education, not personalized investment advice, and partners with licensed providers for savings products.
target_audience: OFWs in Middle East, Hong Kong, Singapore, and worldwide; Filipino workers planning to go abroad; OFW families managing finances together
pricing: Free content / ₱199/mo for premium (PH pricing)
competitors: GCash; Maya; Wise; OWWA financial literacy programs
competitor_gap: Host-country-specific budgeting and savings goals in Tagalog, linked to the family back home
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): I send money home but don't track if it's being used well | Exchange rates vary but I don't have time to compare | I want to save for return but keep dipping into savings | Coordinating finances with family back home is difficult
unique_data_capture: OFW income, remittance frequency, corridor costs and savings-goal outcomes by host country
commoditization_risk: Medium: GCash and Maya serve OFWs, Wise compares rates, and general AI assistants help budget
regulatory_notes: Financial-advice limits; investment products sold need SEC/BSP licensing; Data Privacy Act
founder_feasibility: Yes as an offshore SaaS billed by card/e-wallet; local entity or partner needed for some payment rails and B2B invoicing.
mvp_features: Budget planner + rate comparator + family coordinator + savings tracker
review_notes: Large audience but weak willingness to pay; monetization likely via affiliate, which raises advice-licensing questions.
score_justification: L4 AI budgets and compares remittance options; E4; A4 millions of OFWs; P3 OFW Facebook groups; M3 remittance and budget patterns; W2 OFWs are price-sensitive and GCash is free

title: SEA SMELoan Finder
tagline: SME financing content + AI that matches small businesses with appropriate lenders across SEA markets
target_segment: SME owners in Philippines/Indonesia/Malaysia/Thailand seeking growth capital
problem: Small businesses in the Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand struggle to get credit: banks reject them for lack of collateral, P2P and online lenders charge high rates, and government SME loan schemes are hard to find and understand. Owners apply blindly and collect rejections that hurt their credit.
solution: An SME financing matcher that asks about revenue, years operating, documents and need, then shows which banks, licensed online lenders and government schemes the business is likely to qualify for, with estimated rates and requirements. It prepares a document checklist and a simple financial summary for applications. Lenders pay a success fee on funded loans, disclosed to the borrower. Data is shared only with consent.
target_audience: SME owners in Philippines/Indonesia/Malaysia/Thailand seeking growth capital
pricing: Free business assessment / Success fee on approved loans (typically 1-2%)
competitors: Lendela; Funding Societies; First Circle; Bank SME portals
competitor_gap: Neutral matching that includes government SME schemes alongside private lenders in each market
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): I don't know which government programs I qualify for | I don't know how to present my business properly
unique_data_capture: SME financial profiles matched to lender decisions, rates offered and reasons for rejection, by country and lender
commoditization_risk: Medium: Lendela, Funding Societies and bank marketplaces already match SMEs to loans
regulatory_notes: Loan brokering and lead-gen may need licensing (OJK in Indonesia, SEC/BSP in the Philippines); fee disclosure; credit data privacy
founder_feasibility: Hard solo: lender partnerships and licensing per country.
mvp_features: Business health assessor | Government program eligibility checker | Lender matching algorithm | Application document preparer | Loan comparison calculator
review_notes: Strong WTP from lenders but regulatory licensing in each country is the gating risk.
score_justification: L3 matching is rules plus scoring; E3 lender partnerships take time; A4 SME credit gap is large; P2 SME channel is fragmented; M4 application and approval data compound; W4 lenders pay success fees

title: DTIBIR Helper
tagline: Philippine business registration content + AI that guides entrepreneurs through DTI/BIR/Mayor's permit maze
problem: Starting a business in the Philippines means DTI or SEC registration, barangay clearance, a Mayor's permit and BIR registration, with requirements and fees that differ by city. Many entrepreneurs pay agents thousands of pesos or stay informal, and mistakes lead to penalties or rejected applications. Rules such as BIR registration also changed in 2024.
solution: A guided registration assistant: the user picks business type, structure and city, and gets an exact step-by-step path covering DTI or SEC, barangay, Mayor's permit, BIR registration and books of accounts, with current fees, documents and office tips for that LGU. It pre-fills forms, checks uploaded documents for common errors and tracks each step. Users report actual fees and processing times, which keeps the LGU map current. Upsells include bookkeeping and tax-filing partners.
target_audience: Filipino entrepreneurs starting businesses; existing informal businesses wanting to formalize; side hustlers going legitimate; SMEs registering additional businesses
pricing: Free requirement checker / ₱499 DIY guide / ₱2,999 with document review
competitors: DTI BNRS; BIR ORUS; eGov PH; Taxumo; Registration agents
competitor_gap: Agents are costly and opaque; government portals cover their own step but not the full DTI/SEC-BIR-LGU-barangay sequence for a specific city
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): I don't know which comes first - DTI or BIR | I keep getting rejected for missing documents
unique_data_capture: City- and barangay-level permit requirements, fees, processing times and rejection reasons reported by users, giving the only maintained LGU requirement map
commoditization_risk: Medium: DTI, BIR and the eGov PH app offer online steps, and general AI assistants explain them, but local LGU requirements vary and are poorly documented
regulatory_notes: The Ease of Paying Taxes Act (RA 11976, 2024) changed BIR registration (e.g. removing the annual registration fee), so content must be kept current; document review must not stray into legal advice; Data Privacy Act
founder_feasibility: Yes as an offshore SaaS billed by card/e-wallet; local entity or partner needed for some payment rails and B2B invoicing. Foreign founder can run it as an offshore SaaS with a local content partner.
mvp_features: Step-by-step registration wizard | Document requirement checker by business type | Form auto-filler | Application status tracker | LGU-specific requirement database
review_notes: Good wedge with a compounding LGU dataset; must keep up with BIR and LGU rule changes and upsell to bookkeeping/tax filing partners.
score_justification: L4 AI builds a requirement path by business type and LGU; E4 guided flow plus document templates in weeks; A4 large demand to register and formalize; P3 Filipino entrepreneur Facebook groups and TikTok; M4 LGU-by-LGU requirement and fee data compounds; W3 Filipinos already pay agents ₱5,000-20,000 (est.) for registration

title: IndonesiaOSS Helper
tagline: Indonesian OSS business licensing content + AI that navigates the complex NIB and KBLI system
target_segment: Indonesian entrepreneurs and SMEs needing business licenses
problem: Indonesian entrepreneurs must get an NIB through the OSS risk-based licensing system, choosing the right KBLI business codes and risk level. Wrong codes lead to rejected applications, missing permits or the wrong obligations, and the rules were revised in 2025. Legal service firms charge high fees for what many see as paperwork.
solution: A Bahasa Indonesia assistant where users describe their business in plain words, and the AI suggests the right KBLI codes with explanations, shows the risk level and required permits, and walks through the OSS application step by step with a document checklist. It tracks follow-up permits and flags when rule changes affect their codes. Complex cases are referred to partner legal firms. Pricing is a one-off fee per NIB.
target_audience: Indonesian entrepreneurs and SMEs needing business licenses
pricing: Rp150k DIY / Rp750k with review
competitors: OSS RBA portal; Easybiz; Kontrak Hukum; Legal consultants
competitor_gap: Low-cost self-serve KBLI selection and checklist for micro businesses that legal firms price out
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): I don't know which KBLI code fits my business | My NIB application keeps getting rejected
unique_data_capture: Business descriptions mapped to chosen KBLI codes, risk levels and OSS approval or rejection outcomes
commoditization_risk: Medium: OSS itself, legal-service startups like Easybiz and Kontrak Hukum, and general AI suggest KBLI codes
regulatory_notes: Risk-based licensing rules were revised in 2025 (PP 28/2025 replacing PP 5/2021), so mapping must be updated; legal services need licensed advocates for disputes
founder_feasibility: Needs an Indonesian partner for local payments and legal escalation.
mvp_features: Interactive KBLI finder and checklist generator
review_notes: Useful but competes with legal-service startups and free OSS guidance; regulation churn is high.
score_justification: L4 AI suggests KBLI codes and steps; E3 regulation mapping; A4 many Indonesian SMEs need NIB; P3 TikTok/Instagram; M3 KBLI selection and approval outcomes; W3 SMEs pay legal service firms

title: SEA Freelancer Tax
tagline: SEA freelancer content + AI that helps gig workers and freelancers handle taxes across different SEA countries
target_segment: Freelancers in Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam
problem: Freelancers and gig workers across Southeast Asia, including Upwork contractors, Grab drivers and content creators, often do not know whether or how to file taxes, especially on foreign income. Rules differ by country and changed recently, such as Thailand taxing foreign income remitted from 2024. Unfiled returns lead to penalties.
solution: A tax-obligation assistant for SEA freelancers: users enter country, income sources and amounts, and the AI explains which taxes apply, estimates what they owe and builds a filing calendar. Income is logged through bank and platform exports. Partner tax agents handle filing for a fee where rules require it. It starts with the Philippines and Thailand. Income data is stored under PDPA and DPA rules. Subscriptions include a filing calendar and reminders, and filing help is a separate fee.
target_audience: Freelancers in Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam; gig workers on Grab, Gojek; remote workers for international companies; content creators with multiple income sources
pricing: Free calculator / $15 monthly with filing help
competitors: Taxumo; JuanTax; Revenue department e-filing; General AI assistants
competitor_gap: Multi-country rules for freelancers paid by foreign platforms in TH, VN, ID and MY
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): I don't know if I need to pay taxes on my Upwork income | I don't know how to categorize my different income sources
unique_data_capture: Freelancer income sources (local, foreign platforms, crypto) mapped to filing outcomes and penalties by country
commoditization_risk: Medium: Taxumo serves Philippine freelancers; revenue departments publish guides; general AI explains rules but misses local detail
regulatory_notes: Tax advice liability; Thailand's 2024 rule taxing foreign income remitted into Thailand (Por. 161/2566) changed obligations; filing services may need registered tax agents
founder_feasibility: Yes as an offshore SaaS billed by card/e-wallet; local entity or partner needed for some payment rails and B2B invoicing.
mvp_features: Spreadsheet calculator + guide documents
review_notes: Tax-advice liability and per-country rule upkeep; start with one country.
score_justification: L4 AI explains obligations by country; E3 per-country tax rules; A4 growing freelancer base; P3 freelancer Facebook groups; M3 income-type and filing data; W3 freelancers pay Taxumo-like tools

title: Virtual Assistant SEA
tagline: VA training content + AI that helps Filipinos land and excel at virtual assistant jobs for international clients
problem: The Philippines is a major virtual assistant hub, but competition for international clients is fierce and many aspiring VAs fail to land or keep jobs because of skill gaps in communication, tools and client management. AI tools now automate basic admin tasks, so clients expect VAs to do more.
solution: A VA career platform for Filipinos that assesses skills, trains in-demand areas such as AI tool operation, automation, customer support and bookkeeping basics, and runs AI mock client interviews with feedback on English and professionalism. Graduates get a verified skills profile and introductions to vetted clients. Placement and rate outcomes are tracked to improve the curriculum. Courses are paid upfront with optional monthly job support.
target_audience: Filipinos wanting to become VAs; existing VAs wanting to upskill and increase rates; career changers seeking remote work; fresh graduates entering VA industry
pricing: ₱1999 course / ₱499 monthly job support
competitors: OnlineJobs.ph; Upwork; VA training academies; Free YouTube courses
competitor_gap: Skills training focused on AI-augmented VA work (automation, AI tool operation) with verified placement data
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): I apply to hundreds of VA jobs but never hear back | I don't know what skills international clients actually want | My English is good but I struggle in interviews | I landed a job but don't know how to use the tools they want | I want to increase my rate but don't know how to upskill
unique_data_capture: VA skill assessments and mock-interview scores linked to placement, client type and hourly rate achieved
commoditization_risk: Medium: many VA academies, free YouTube training and OnlineJobs.ph exist; AI agents automate basic VA tasks
regulatory_notes: Job placement for foreign clients may need DOLE/DMW recruitment licensing; consumer protection for course claims
founder_feasibility: Yes as an offshore SaaS billed by card/e-wallet; local entity or partner needed for some payment rails and B2B invoicing.
mvp_features: Skills gap assessor | Training modules for in-demand skills | Mock interview simulator | Job matching with vetted clients | AI work assistant for on-the-job support
review_notes: Crowded course market, and AI is eroding demand for basic VA tasks; must retrain VAs for AI-augmented roles.
score_justification: L4 AI trains and mock-interviews; E3 course plus job-matching flows; A4 large PH VA workforce; P3 Facebook VA groups; M3 skill assessments and placement outcomes; W3 Filipinos pay for VA courses

title: ReviewerPH
tagline: Philippine board exam content + AI that creates personalized review materials for licensure exams
target_segment: Filipino professionals preparing for PRC licensure examinations
problem: Every year many Filipinos sit PRC licensure exams for nursing, teaching, accountancy and engineering, and many pay review centers tens of thousands of pesos (est.) for months of classes. Review centers teach everyone the same way, and examinees cannot tell which topics will cost them the exam. Failing means waiting months to retake.
solution: An adaptive board-exam reviewer: a diagnostic test maps each examinee's weak topics against the PRC table of specifications, then the app serves practice questions written and reviewed by licensed professionals, with AI-generated variants and explanations. It schedules spaced review until exam day, runs timed mock exams and shows a pass-probability estimate by topic. Results reported after the exam calibrate question difficulty for the next cohort.
target_audience: Filipino professionals preparing for PRC licensure examinations
pricing: ₱499/month for single exam / ₱799/month for comprehensive with mock exams / ₱1,499 for intensive 3-month package
competitors: Review centers (e.g. for nursing, LET, CPA); Quizlet; Reviewer apps; Facebook reviewer groups
competitor_gap: Review centers are costly and one-size-fits-all; apps lack adaptivity and pass-probability tracking by topic
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): I failed before and don't know what to focus on | I work and can't attend scheduled review classes | I need practice questions but quality ones are limited
unique_data_capture: Item-level answer data by exam, topic and examinee, with later pass/fail results reported, giving difficulty calibration and pass-probability predictions per board exam
commoditization_risk: Medium: general AI can quiz on topics, but calibrated board-exam-style item banks and pass prediction need exam-specific data
regulatory_notes: Must not reproduce actual PRC exam questions (leaking exam items is prohibited); copyright in review-center materials; Data Privacy Act
founder_feasibility: Yes as an offshore SaaS billed by card/e-wallet; local entity or partner needed for some payment rails and B2B invoicing. Subject-matter reviewers needed per exam.
mvp_features: Diagnostic weak area identifier | AI-generated practice questions by topic | Personalized study plan | Mock exam simulator | Performance tracker with readiness score
review_notes: Clear WTP and data moat; quality control of AI-generated items and avoiding leaked questions are the main risks.
score_justification: L4 AI generates practice items and adapts to weak areas; E4 question bank plus adaptive engine in weeks; A4 large yearly PRC exam cohorts (nursing, LET, CPA, engineering); P3 reviewer Facebook groups and TikTok; M4 item-level performance data compounds; W3 examinees already pay review centers far more

title: Thai English Pro

title: PAG-IBIG Housing Helper

title: Halal Cert SEA
tagline: Halal certification content + AI that guides F&B businesses through halal certification process in Malaysia/Indonesia
problem: Food businesses applying for halal certification in Malaysia (JAKIM) or Indonesia (BPJPH) must assemble ingredient lists, supplier halal certificates, process flows and an internal halal assurance system. Indonesia has made halal certification mandatory for most food and beverage products, phased by business size. Small firms find the documentation confusing and often fail first audits on supplier paperwork, paying consultants thousands of ringgit or millions of rupiah (est.).
solution: A halal-readiness workspace: the business lists products, ingredients and suppliers, and the tool checks each ingredient against stored supplier certificates and expiries, flags gaps, and generates the document set each regime expects (ingredient matrix, process flow, halal assurance manual drafts). It produces a pre-audit checklist in Malay, Bahasa Indonesia or English and reminds the firm before supplier certificates expire. It does not certify; it prepares the submission for MYeHALAL or SIHALAL. It beats consultants on price and keeps working after certification for renewals.
target_audience: F&B businesses seeking halal certification; restaurants wanting halal status; food manufacturers; international brands entering MY/ID market
pricing: RM299 / Rp1.5M one-off readiness pack; RM79 / Rp350k monthly for certificate tracking
competitors: Halal consultants in MY and ID; JAKIM MYeHALAL portal; BPJPH SIHALAL; ChatGPT
competitor_gap: Consultants are manual and expensive; portals accept applications but do not help prepare them
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): I don't know what documentation I need to prepare | My supply chain halal compliance is unclear
unique_data_capture: A supplier-ingredient registry mapping each raw material and supplier to its halal certificate, issuing body and expiry, reusable across every applicant who uses that supplier
commoditization_risk: Medium: AI assistants can summarise the rules, but cannot track a firm's supplier certificates and expiries
regulatory_notes: Must stay consistent with JAKIM (MYeHALAL) and BPJPH (SIHALAL) procedures; cannot certify, only prepare. Indonesia's free self-declare route for micro firms limits the low end
founder_feasibility: Solo founder can build the document workflow; Indonesian market needs a local partner for sales and Bahasa content
mvp_features: Certification requirement checker (JAKIM/BPJPH) | Document preparation wizard | Supply chain compliance tracker | Audit preparation guide | Common failure point alerter
review_notes: The open question is whether small and mid F&B firms will pay once Indonesia's micro-business free self-declare route and post-deadline enforcement settle.
score_justification: L4 LLM maps documents and supplier certs to requirements; E3 two regimes (JAKIM, BPJPH) to encode; A4 Indonesia's mandatory halal certification for F&B drives demand; P3 F&B associations and Facebook groups; M3 supplier halal-cert database; W4 firms already pay consultants

title: Travel Nurse Helper
tagline: Travel nursing content + AI that helps travel nurses find contracts and manage multi-state licensing
problem: Travel nurses compare offers from several agencies that package pay differently (taxable base vs untaxed stipends, guaranteed hours, cancellation terms). They also hold licences in several states, track compact status and renewal dates, and must keep a valid tax home to keep stipends untaxed. Mistakes cost thousands in tax or lost contracts.
solution: Navigate travel nursing with an AI assistant that compares contracts across agencies, accounting for total compensation including housing stipends, travel reimbursement, and benefits. The system tracks your multi-state licensing status, alerts you to compact state changes, and provides tax home guidance to ensure you're maximizing your tax-free stipends legally. Includes contract red flag detection and negotiation talking points.
target_audience: Travel nurses; nursing staffing agency contractors; healthcare travelers
pricing: Free comparison / $19.99 monthly
competitors: Vivian; Trusted Health; travel tax specialists; Nurse Licensure Compact site
competitor_gap: Marketplaces show listings, not neutral comparisons of a nurse's actual offers and licence pipeline
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): I don't know which agency offers the best package
unique_data_capture: Submitted contract offers itemised into base pay, stipends and hours by agency, facility and state, plus licence processing times by board, compounding into a pay and licensing benchmark
commoditization_risk: Medium: Vivian and Trusted publish contract listings; AI assistants can explain tax-home rules but not live offers
regulatory_notes: Tax-home and stipend guidance is tax advice; refer to tax professionals. Licensing info must track Nurse Licensure Compact changes
founder_feasibility: Solo-buildable; tax content needs review by a tax professional
mvp_features: Contract comparator and license tracker and tax home guide
review_notes: Well-funded marketplaces already compare contracts, so the licence tracker and offer comparison must be clearly better.
score_justification: L3 LLM compares contracts and stipends; E3 multi-state rules; A4 large travel-nurse population; P3 Facebook groups and r/TravelNursing; M3 contract-offer data; W4 nurses pay for tax and licence help

title: Estate Sale Runner
tagline: Estate sale content + AI that helps estate sale companies price items and manage sales efficiently
problem: Estate sale companies must price thousands of mixed items, from furniture and kitchenware to jewellery, art and collectibles, in two or three days before a sale. Under-pricing a valuable item loses money for the family and the company, and researching comps item by item takes too long. Staff often miss items they do not recognise.
solution: A mobile pricing tool for estate sale teams: staff photograph items or whole shelves, and the app identifies objects, flags potentially valuable ones for a closer look, and suggests a price range from online sold comps blended with realized estate-sale prices from other users. It prints price tags or QR labels, builds the item list for the sale listing, and records final sale prices and discounts by day. That realized-price feedback makes the suggestions better than one-item comp tools. Sale-day reports show sell-through by category.
target_audience: Estate sale companies; liquidators; antique dealers
pricing: Free trial; $49 monthly per company or $1 per 100 items priced
competitors: WorthPoint; EstateSales.NET; Google Lens; ChatGPT; PriceCharting for collectibles
competitor_gap: Comp tools are built for one item at a time and use online sold prices, not estate-sale realized prices
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): I miss valuable items because I don't recognize them
unique_data_capture: Realized sale prices from estate sales by item category, condition, region and sale day (including day-two discounts), which marketplaces never see because the items sell offline
commoditization_risk: Medium: Google Lens and AI assistants can identify single items, but not price a 2,000-item house quickly with local realized prices
regulatory_notes: Item valuation is not a regulated appraisal; avoid calling it an appraisal for estate or tax purposes
founder_feasibility: Solo-buildable; sell through estate sale company associations and EstateSales.NET company groups
mvp_features: Photo-based item identifier, pricing database with recent sales comps, sale organizer by room/category, tag generator, sold item tracker
review_notes: Main risk is that a listing platform such as EstateSales.NET adds similar pricing tools; realized-price data is the defence.
score_justification: L4 vision identifies items and pulls comps; E3 photo-to-price pipeline plus tagging in about 4 weeks; A3 thousands of estate sale firms (est.); P3 EstateSales.NET company base and Facebook groups; M4 realized-price data compounds; W4 firms earn commissions and pay for tools

title: Reptile Breeder
tagline: Reptile breeding content + AI that helps breeders track genetics, manage colonies and plan pairings
problem: Ball python, leopard gecko and other morph breeders keep dozens or hundreds of animals and track complex genetics, including recessive, co-dominant and het-possible traits. Records live in spreadsheets, so planning pairings to hit a target morph, proving hets and tracking clutches and incubation is error-prone. Mistakes cost a breeding season.
solution: Colony software for morph breeders: each animal gets a record with lineage, visual and het genes, weights and feedings. A pairing planner calculates expected offspring for any pair and suggests pairings to reach a target morph over one or two seasons. Clutch, incubation and hatch records update het-proven status automatically, and listings can be pushed to marketplaces. Aggregated clutch outcomes across breeders show how real hatch ratios compare with theory.
target_audience: Reptile breeders; ball python morphers; gecko breeders
pricing: Free basics / $19.99 monthly
competitors: MorphMarket; Herpstat; breeder spreadsheets
competitor_gap: Marketplace tools are tied to listings; few breeders track pairings and clutches cleanly
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): I want specific morphs but don't know which pairings
unique_data_capture: Per-pairing clutch outcomes (actual morph ratios hatched, het-proven animals) across breeders, which tests real inheritance against theory
commoditization_risk: Medium: MorphMarket offers a genetics calculator and breeder tools; general AI assistants calculate Punnett squares
regulatory_notes: Wildlife and reptile trade rules vary by state and country; CITES for some species
founder_feasibility: Solo-buildable
mvp_features: Colony manager and genetic calculator and pairing planner
review_notes: MorphMarket already owns breeder workflows and its calculator, so this needs a better colony-records product to stand out.
score_justification: L4 genetics calculations; E4 Punnett-style calculator in a week; A3 morph breeders; P3 MorphMarket and Facebook groups; M3 pairing and clutch outcomes; W3 breeders pay for marketplace tools

title: Junk Removal Biz
tagline: Junk removal content + AI that helps operators price jobs and optimize routes
target_segment: Junk removal business owners and operators
problem: Junk removal operators quote jobs by eye or from customer photos, and under-quoting volume, weight or dump fees wipes out the profit on a job. Customers want an instant price before booking, but sending a truck for an estimate wastes time. Operators also miss resale value in what they haul.
solution: A photo-quoting tool for junk haulers: customers upload photos through a booking link, and the system estimates truck-load fraction, flags heavy or specially regulated items (mattresses, e-waste, tyres), and suggests a price that includes local dump fees. After the job the crew records actual volume and fees, so estimates improve per operator. It plans routes to transfer stations and resale drop-offs and syncs jobs into Jobber or Housecall Pro. Resale finds are logged for extra margin.
target_audience: Junk removal business owners and operators
pricing: Free trial; $49 monthly per truck
competitors: Jobber; Housecall Pro; junk-removal franchise software; manual photo quoting
competitor_gap: Generic field-service tools do not estimate load volume or disposal cost from photos
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): I underquote jobs and lose money
unique_data_capture: Paired customer photos and the actual truck volume, weight, dump fees and resale items for each job, which trains volume estimates and shows margin per job type
commoditization_risk: Medium: Jobber and similar field-service tools add generic AI quoting, but not photo-based junk volume and disposal-cost estimation
regulatory_notes: Disposal rules for e-waste, mattresses, tyres and hazardous items vary by state; must flag them
founder_feasibility: Solo-buildable; sell in owner Facebook groups and integrate with Jobber
mvp_features: Photo pricer and route optimizer and disposal guide
review_notes: Key risk is Jobber or Housecall Pro adding photo volume estimation; owning the photo-vs-actual dataset is the defence.
score_justification: L4 vision estimates truck-load volume and item mix from customer photos; E3 photo-to-quote MVP in about 4 weeks; A3 many independent junk haulers (est.); P3 franchise and owner Facebook groups; M4 photo-vs-actual-load data compounds; W4 operators pay for field-service software

title: Daycare Inspector
tagline: Daycare reviews with violation history - what parents actually need to know
problem: Parents choosing a daycare for an infant or toddler have very little reliable information. State licensing agencies publish inspection and violation reports, but they sit in hard-to-search PDFs that vary by state. Serious citations, such as ratio violations, unsafe sleep and abuse findings, are mixed in with paperwork lapses. Most parents decide on a tour and a few online reviews.
solution: A daycare directory that ingests state licensing inspection reports and uses an LLM to classify each citation by severity and category, from paperwork to supervision to safety. Every provider shows a plain-English violation timeline, its repeat-violation pattern, staff ratios, openings and tuition ranges. Parent reviews come from verified enrolled families. Alerts tell subscribed parents when a new inspection is posted, and providers can claim profiles to post openings and responses.
target_audience: Parents of young children; expecting parents; corporate relocation services
business_model: Freemium + Daycare Subscriptions (Daycare premium profiles, corporate partnerships, data licensing)
pricing: Free to search / $49/mo for daycares to respond and add info
competitors: Winnie; Care.com; state childcare licensing portals; Childcare Aware
competitor_gap: State portals are hard to use, and Winnie's inspection coverage is uneven; few rank violations by severity.
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): Daycare violations near me | Is this daycare safe | Daycare reviews and ratings
unique_data_capture: A normalised, multi-state database of daycare inspection citations by severity and date, linked to licence numbers and parent reviews, including the rate of repeat violations.
commoditization_risk: Medium: Winnie and state portals already show some inspection data.
regulatory_notes: Public records are fine; present citations accurately to avoid defamation.
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible starting with 3–5 states that have structured data.
mvp_features: Inspection data integration, parent reviews, daycare profiles, violation alerts, waitlist info
review_notes: Winnie is a well-funded direct competitor; the edge must be a better inspection-data layer.
score_justification: L4 LLM parses state inspection reports; E3 50 different state data formats; A4 parents search heavily; P3 SEO and parent groups; M4 normalised violation history compounds; W3 providers pay for enrolment leads

title: Senior Care Match
tagline: Find senior care with real family reviews and inspection scores
problem: Adult children choosing assisted living, memory care or a nursing home for a parent usually decide in a crisis, within days. The best-known finders are paid by the facilities they recommend, so families get sales calls instead of neutral advice. Inspection reports and staffing data exist but are scattered across CMS and 50 state agencies.
solution: An independent senior-care directory that merges CMS Care Compare ratings, staffing levels and inspection citations with state assisted-living records and verified family reviews. An LLM writes a plain-English risk summary for each facility and flags recent serious citations. Families filter by care level, Medicaid acceptance, memory-care capability and reported monthly price. Facilities pay for enhanced profiles, not placement fees, and the site says so clearly. The result is a neutral view that referral-fee sites cannot offer.
target_audience: Adult children of aging parents; hospital discharge planners; elder law attorneys
business_model: Lead Gen + Subscriptions (Facility subscriptions, referral fees, premium placements)
pricing: Free to search / $199/mo facility subscriptions
competitors: A Place for Mom; Caring.com; Medicare Care Compare; Seniorly
competitor_gap: Incumbents are paid by facilities, which biases recommendations; assisted-living inspection data is rarely surfaced.
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): Nursing home reviews | Assisted living near me with good reviews | Memory care ratings
unique_data_capture: Facility-level timelines merging CMS Care Compare staffing and inspection data, state assisted-living citations and verified family reviews, with price quotes families report.
commoditization_risk: High: A Place for Mom and Caring.com dominate with referral-fee models; Medicare Care Compare is free.
regulatory_notes: Referral-fee disclosure laws (e.g. some states regulate senior placement agencies); HIPAA not triggered by public data.
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible as a content-plus-data site; a call-centre referral model is not.
mvp_features: Facility profiles, inspection data, family reviews, pricing transparency, care level matching
review_notes: A Place for Mom is paid by communities, so an independent site needs a non-referral model to stand out, which limits revenue.
score_justification: L3 LLM summarises CMS inspection data; E3 data feeds exist but integration work; A4 very high family search intent; P3 SEO; incumbents dominate ads; M3 inspection plus family reviews; W4 facilities pay large referral fees

title: Funeral Price Compare
tagline: Compare funeral home prices - transparency when families need it most
problem: Families arranging a funeral make many decisions within 48 hours of a death, often without knowing prices. Funeral homes must give an itemised price list on request under the FTC Funeral Rule, but many still do not post prices online. Costs for the same service can differ several-fold in one city, and corporate owners often keep local family names.
solution: A funeral price directory that collects General Price Lists from websites and mystery-shopper requests, then uses an LLM to extract each line item into a standard format. Families compare direct cremation, burial packages, embalming and casket prices, and see the corporate owner behind each home. A price-history view shows increases over time. Homes that post full prices online earn a transparency badge and can pay for a premium profile.
target_audience: Families planning funerals; pre-need planners; hospice workers helping families
business_model: Freemium + Funeral Home Listings (Funeral home subscriptions, pre-need planning partnerships, memorial product affiliates)
pricing: Free to search / $149/mo for funeral homes
competitors: Funeralocity; Parting; Everdays; Google Maps
competitor_gap: Price comparisons exist but rarely flag corporate ownership or line-item history.
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): How much does a funeral cost | Funeral home prices near me | Affordable cremation
unique_data_capture: A time series of funeral-home General Price List line items (direct cremation, embalming, casket markup) by home and corporate owner, gathered from posted and requested GPLs.
commoditization_risk: Medium: Funeralocity and Parting already compare prices.
regulatory_notes: FTC Funeral Rule requires itemised GPLs on request; the FTC has been reviewing online-price rules, so check the rule's current status.
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible; data collection by mystery-shopper requests is laborious.
mvp_features: Funeral home profiles, itemized pricing, family reviews, pre-need planning tools, price comparison
review_notes: Funeralocity and Parting already compare prices, so differentiation must come from line-item depth and corporate-owner flags.
score_justification: L3 LLM extracts General Price List items; E4 scrape posted GPLs; A3 low volume but urgent need; P3 SEO on 'cremation cost [city]'; M4 GPL price history per home; W3 homes pay modestly; affiliates exist

title: Financial Advisor Check
tagline: Find fiduciary advisors with transparent fee disclosure
problem: People looking for a financial advisor cannot easily tell fiduciaries from commission salespeople, or compare what they will really pay. Fees are buried in Form ADV PDFs, and percentage-of-assets fees cost far more over time than most clients realise. Lead-gen matching sites are paid by advisors, so they rarely highlight conflicts of interest.
solution: An advisor directory built on SEC IAPD and FINRA BrokerCheck data. An LLM parses each firm's Form ADV fee schedule into a standard all-in annual cost at $250K, $1M and $3M portfolios. Profiles show fiduciary status, compensation type, conflicts and disciplinary history. Users filter by fee-only, flat-fee, minimums and specialties such as equity compensation or retirement planning. Advisors pay for enhanced profiles, while the fee data stays free and neutral.
target_audience: High-net-worth individuals; pre-retirees; business owners planning exits
business_model: Freemium + Advisor Subscriptions (Advisor subscriptions, lead fees, fintech platform partnerships)
pricing: Free to search / $99/mo advisor profiles
competitors: SmartAsset SmartAdvisor; Wealthtender; NAPFA; FINRA BrokerCheck; SEC IAPD
competitor_gap: Few tools turn Form ADV fee schedules into comparable all-in costs.
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): Fee-only financial advisor near me | Fiduciary advisor | How to find a good financial advisor
unique_data_capture: Parsed Form ADV Part 2 fee schedules, conflicts and disciplinary history for every RIA, normalised into all-in cost at standard portfolio sizes.
commoditization_risk: Medium: SmartAsset, Wealthtender and NAPFA already list advisors; IAPD and BrokerCheck are free.
regulatory_notes: SEC marketing rule affects advisor testimonials; avoid investment advice.
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible; SEC data is public and structured.
mvp_features: Advisor profiles, fee transparency, credential verification, client reviews, minimum filtering
review_notes: Strong data angle, but SmartAsset dominates paid leads; the moat is fee normalisation.
score_justification: L3 LLM parses Form ADV fee schedules; E4 SEC bulk data is free; A4 strong search intent; P3 SEO on 'fee-only advisor [city]'; M3 parsed fee and conflict data; W4 advisors pay $100+ per lead

title: Nutritionist Directory
tagline: Find dietitians by condition specialty - IBS, PCOS, diabetes, and more
problem: People with IBS, PCOS, diabetes, eating disorders or those taking GLP-1 drugs need a dietitian with deep experience in that condition. Generic nutrition advice can make symptoms worse. Search results mix registered dietitians with unlicensed coaches, and insurance coverage is unclear.
solution: A dietitian directory searchable by condition, with verified RD credentials and condition-specific training such as Monash FODMAP or certified diabetes educator. Profiles show which insurance plans are accepted, telehealth states and session prices. An intake form suggests matches based on the condition and coverage. Dietitians pay a monthly listing fee, and condition guides drive search traffic. Each profile also lists the conditions the dietitian does not treat.
target_audience: People with specific health conditions; doctors making referrals; health coaches
business_model: Freemium + Dietitian Subscriptions (Dietitian subscriptions, lead fees, telehealth partnerships)
pricing: Free to search / $39/mo dietitian profiles
competitors: Fay; Nourish; Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics Find a Nutrition Expert; Healthie
competitor_gap: Insurance-telehealth marketplaces already match by condition.
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): Dietitian for PCOS | IBS nutritionist near me | Diabetes dietitian covered by insurance
unique_data_capture: Condition-specific caseload data per dietitian (IBS/low-FODMAP, PCOS, GLP-1 users) and insurance acceptance by plan.
commoditization_risk: High: Fay, Nourish and Berry Street offer insurance-covered dietitians; Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics has Find an Expert.
regulatory_notes: State licensure for dietitians; telehealth across state lines needs licences.
founder_feasibility: Yes, a solo founder can launch it with scraped and claimed listings; sales to listed businesses is the main time cost.
mvp_features: Dietitian profiles, condition specialty tags, approach descriptions, insurance info, virtual options
review_notes: VC-funded insurance-covered marketplaces (Fay, Nourish) now do condition matching for free to patients.
score_justification: L3 LLM matches condition to specialty; E4 easy listing; A4 condition-specific searches are strong; P3 SEO by condition; M3 condition experience data; W3 dietitians pay modestly

title: Addiction Treatment Real
tagline: Find addiction treatment with real outcome data - not marketing claims
problem: Families searching for addiction treatment, often in a crisis, face a market with predatory marketing, call centres that sell leads to the highest bidder, and centres that make outcome claims with no proof. Licensing and accreditation status is hard to check. Choosing badly can cost lives as well as money.
solution: An addiction treatment directory built on SAMHSA locator data, state licensing records and Joint Commission or CARF accreditation, with clear flags for medication-assisted treatment and insurance acceptance. Profiles show ownership history and any regulatory actions. Verified alumni and families leave structured reviews. Centres pay only a flat listing fee, never per referral, to comply with patient-brokering laws.
target_audience: People seeking addiction treatment; families; interventionists; primary care making referrals
business_model: Freemium + Treatment Center Listings (Treatment center subscriptions, intervention service partnerships, recovery coaching affiliates)
pricing: Free to search / $199/mo treatment center profiles
competitors: FindTreatment.gov (SAMHSA); Recovery.com; Rehabs.com; Psychology Today
competitor_gap: Free government locator lacks quality and outcome data; commercial sites are tied to centres.
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): Rehab centers with good success rates | Addiction treatment that works | Alcohol rehab reviews
unique_data_capture: Facility licensing, accreditation, medication-assisted treatment availability and ownership changes, merged with SAMHSA locator data and verified alumni outcomes.
commoditization_risk: Medium: SAMHSA FindTreatment.gov is free; Recovery.com and Rehabs.com exist.
regulatory_notes: Heavy: EKRA and state patient-brokering laws ban paying for referrals; LegitScript certification needed for ads; HIPAA/42 CFR Part 2.
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible only as an information site; any referral-fee model creates legal risk.
mvp_features: Treatment center profiles, outcome data, accreditation verification, family reviews, insurance info
review_notes: Patient-brokering laws make the lead-gen model risky; revenue must be flat-fee listings.
score_justification: L3 LLM parses licensing and accreditation data; E3 regulated, slow build; A4 very high demand; P2 Google restricts rehab ads; M4 verified licensing and outcome data; W4 centres pay a lot, but regulated

title: Content Creator Rates
tagline: Influencer rate directory - know what to pay before you negotiate
problem: Brands and creators negotiate sponsorships with no shared idea of fair pricing. Small creators often undercharge, while brands overpay for creators with inflated followings. Most rate calculators are guesses based on follower counts. Agencies spend hours on rate negotiations that a benchmark could settle in minutes.
solution: An influencer rate directory built from verified deal submissions, where creators upload a redacted contract or invoice. Rates are shown by platform, niche, follower band, engagement and deliverable type. Brands subscribe for benchmark reports and creator search. Creators get free access in exchange for contributing data, so the dataset grows with use. Rate trends are published quarterly by niche, so both sides can see how prices move over time.
target_audience: Brands planning influencer campaigns; creators setting rates; agencies pricing deals
business_model: Subscription (Brand subscriptions, agency subscriptions, platform partnerships)
pricing: $49/mo for brands / Free for creators contributing data
competitors: Collabstr; Passionfroot; CreatorIQ; HypeAuditor; FYPM
competitor_gap: Public rates are estimates; few have contract-verified data.
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): How much to pay Instagram influencer | YouTube sponsorship rates | Influencer rate card
unique_data_capture: Verified sponsorship deal rates by platform, follower band, niche and deliverable, submitted with contract proof.
commoditization_risk: Medium: CreatorIQ, Passionfroot, Collabstr and free rate calculators publish benchmarks.
regulatory_notes: None notable
founder_feasibility: Yes, a solo founder can launch it with scraped and claimed listings; sales to listed businesses is the main time cost.
mvp_features: Rate benchmarks by platform/size, anonymized deal data, rate calculator, outreach tools
review_notes: Rate-data niche is real but marketplaces already publish benchmarks.
score_justification: L3 LLM normalises rate data; E4 easy build; A3 creators and brands search rates; P3 creator communities; M4 verified deal-rate data; W3 brands pay for benchmarks
